newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty eases vs basket, depos edge lower.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty eases vs basket, depos edge lower.

text.p: The Polish zloty closed softer against the basket of currencies in light trade as fears of a central bank intervention pushed the market down to resistance levels at three percent from parity, dealers said.

They said banks may be reluctant to test resistance in upcoming days even if the zloty was under appreciation pressure because of more profitable zloty positions and foreign investment in the Warsaw bourse and Polish fixed bonds.
"Banks may be reluctant to test the zloty's upside because there is a high probability of central bank action above three percent from parity," said Tomasz Wolosz, dealer at BRE SA.
The zloty closed at 3.07/3.02 percent from the trading band centre, softer than Monday's 3.13/3.07 percent close.
It was at 3.0730/45 to the dollar, down from 3.0560/70 on Monday and at 1.7987/97 to the mark, up from 1.8045/65.

One-day deposit rates eased slightly after banks received funds from late afternoon clearing-house settlements and were seen trading below 23 percent tomorrow on an expected 400 million zloty net inflow into the system.
O/N rates were at 21.50/22.50 percent, down from opening's 22.70/23.15 percent. Tomorrow/next rates were at 22.00/23.00 percent against 22.85/23.10 percent this morning.
At Wednesday's joint 800 million zloty 12-percent five-year and 15-percent two-year fixed bond tender yields were expected to hold relatively flat at 18.55 and 20.6 percent respectively.

Dealers said large foreign investor entry at tomorrow's tender could give the zloty a boost before the March 12 value date. Foreigners bought the vast majority of the 550 million zlotys of 12-percent five-year bonds sold on February 5.
